immediate_action: Immediately prune and safely discard heavily spotted leaves in dry weather. Avoid working among plants while wet. Disinfect pruning shears in 70% isopropyl alcohol between cuts.
organic_treatment: Apply fixed copper bactericide combined with Bacillus subtilis spray every 7-10 days. Spray cold-pressed neem oil during early morning or dusk to suppress bacterial spread.
chemical_treatment: Copper-based bactericides (e.g. Copper Hydroxide or Copper Sulfate) tank-mixed with Mancozeb to enhance bacterial inhibition where permitted by regional guidelines.
cultural_practices: Space plants 18-24 inches apart to ensure maximum airflow and sunlight penetration. Always irrigate at ground level using drip hoses rather than overhead sprinklers.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free, resistant pepper varieties. Practice a strict 3-year crop rotation avoiding all Solanaceae (tomatoes, potatoes, eggplants). Apply organic mulch around base to prevent soil splash.

immediate_action: Continue standard routine maintenance. Inspect foliage weekly for early signs of pests such as aphids or spider mites.
organic_treatment: Apply diluted organic kelp or fish emulsion foliar feed every 2-3 weeks to promote vigorous root and canopy development.
chemical_treatment: No chemical fungicides or bactericides required. Maintain balanced slow-release N-P-K (5-10-10) fertilizer.
cultural_practices: Ensure 1-1.5 inches of water per week delivered evenly at the root zone. Maintain 2 inches of clean straw or shredded bark mulch to preserve soil moisture.
prevention: Maintain garden sanitation, sanitize stakes and cages at end of season, and foster beneficial predator insects (ladybugs, lacewings).

immediate_action: Prune lower yellowing and spotted leaves that touch or lie near the soil surface. Burn or bag affected foliage; never compost diseased plant parts.
organic_treatment: Spray certified organic copper fungicide or bio-fungicide containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens at first notice of leaf spots. Repeat every 7 days until foliage stabilizes.
chemical_treatment: Preventative applications of Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin applied according to label rates at 7-14 day intervals during warm, wet periods.
cultural_practices: Stake or hill potatoes carefully without injuring root systems. Irrigate early in the morning so sun quickly dries incidental splash moisture on leaves.
prevention: Ensure high soil organic matter and adequate potassium/nitrogen balance to avoid plant stress. Rotate planting beds on a 3 to 4 year cycle. Use certified seed tubers.

immediate_action: URGENT: Immediately remove and destroy all infected foliage and haulm. If widespread in garden, cut down entire above-ground plant to prevent pathogen moving into tubers.
organic_treatment: Copper soap (Copper Octanoate) or OMRI-listed bio-fungicides (Bacillus subtilis). Note: late blight is aggressive and organic options are strictly preventative.
chemical_treatment: Systemic and contact oomycete-targeted fungicides such as Dimethomorph, Fluopicolide, or Cymoxanil tank-mixed with protectant Mancozeb/Chlorothalonil.
cultural_practices: Destroy all potato cull piles and volunteer potato sprouts in the vicinity. Hill soil generously over potato tubers to create a physical protective barrier against washed spores.
prevention: Select resistant cultivars (e.g. Sarpo Mira, Defender). Never save seed tubers from blighted crops. Monitor local blight warning forecasts closely.

immediate_action: No curative action required. Continue routine hilling as tubers grow to prevent greening from sunlight exposure.
organic_treatment: Apply compost tea or foliar seaweed extract periodically to support vigorous vegetative leaf mass.
chemical_treatment: No chemical treatments required. Ensure balanced potassium supply for healthy tuber enlargement.
cultural_practices: Maintain consistent, moderate moisture—avoid waterlogging or extended drought stress. Keep hills weed-free to improve airflow.
prevention: Always source certified seed tubers. Maintain multi-year Solanaceous crop rotation and sanitize agricultural implements.

immediate_action: Remove and destroy infected leaflets during dry weather. Sterilize pruners between every cut using a 10% bleach solution or 70% alcohol.
organic_treatment: Spray preventative liquid copper fungicide combined with bio-fungicide Serenade (Bacillus subtilis) at 7-day intervals.
chemical_treatment: Copper hydroxide bactericide tank-mixed with protectant Mancozeb to overcome copper-tolerant bacterial strains, adhering strictly to pre-harvest intervals.
cultural_practices: Use drip or soaker hose irrigation to keep leaves completely dry. Stake and prune suckers to optimize air circulation through the canopy.
prevention: Purchase hot-water treated or certified disease-free seeds and seedlings. Rotate out of tomato/pepper family for at least 3 years. Mulch heavily beneath plants.

immediate_action: Pinch off infected lower leaflets showing target spots. Dispose in sealed trash; do not leave trimmings on garden soil.
organic_treatment: Apply copper fungicide, sulfur sprays, or potassium bicarbonate solutions every 7 to 10 days, ensuring thorough coverage of both leaf surfaces.
chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb sprays applied proactively before heavy disease establishment; switch to systemic fungicides (e.g. Difenoconazole) if disease spreads.
cultural_practices: Prune off bottom 12 inches of foliage once plant is established to prevent splash contamination from soil. Apply 2-3 inches of straw mulch.
prevention: Choose tolerant hybrid varieties (e.g. Mountain Supreme, Defiant). Disinfect cages and stakes with disinfectant between seasons. Rotate planting location annually.

immediate_action: CRITICAL: Act immediately. Bag and remove infected plants in dry conditions. Disinfect hands and tools immediately to prevent spreading spores to neighbors.
organic_treatment: Liquid copper fungicides can offer preventative protection to unaffected foliage, but will not cure severely blighted tissue.
chemical_treatment: Targeted oomycide chemistry such as Cyazofamid, Mandipropamid, or Chlorothalonil protectant sprays applied on strict schedules during cool, wet weather.
cultural_practices: Avoid late afternoon or evening overhead irrigation. Space plants at least 3 feet apart. Provide greenhouse ventilation or protective row covers during wet spells.
prevention: Plant late blight-resistant varieties (e.g. Defiant Ph-R, Mountain Merit, Legend). Eliminate volunteer tomatoes and nightshade weeds. Check regional blight alerts.

immediate_action: Maintain current care schedule. Monitor underside of leaves weekly for early hornworm or aphid activity.
organic_treatment: Feed with organic worm castings or compost tea every 3-4 weeks. Add calcium (crushed eggshells or gypsum) to prevent blossom end rot.
chemical_treatment: No chemical sprays required. Feed with balanced organic fertilizer suited for fruiting solanaceous crops.
cultural_practices: Stake or trellis vines firmly. Prune lower suckers to promote vertical growth and sunlight absorption. Mulch generously around root zone.
prevention: Rotate planting spots every 3 years. Clean up all crop debris in autumn to deny overwintering habitat for pathogens.
